rundown: Leathernecks beat Storm 90-48 at Western Hall in Macomb, IL in front of 425. Leathernecks led 40-22 at half-time and never looked back. By ESPN's win probability it was never really in doubt (never below 99%).
Leading the way — Storm: Calix Cahill 12 pts; Spencer Holley 2 ast; Isaac Averill 5 reb. Leathernecks: Daivion Traylor 16 pts, 10 reb; Tayelor Moore 2 ast.
Where Leathernecks won it: they shot 47% to 30%, shot 31% from three to 18% and won the boards 43-24.

review.title: The algo's call
review.body:
Logged before the start, last snapshot Nov 9, 6:53 PM ET. It had Storm 79% and Leathernecks 21%, projecting Storm 79.1 – Leathernecks 70.3 (149.4 total, Storm by 8.8).

Final: Storm 48 – Leathernecks 90. Wrong winner: it had Storm at 79%, and Leathernecks (21%) won.

Thin data: 3 of 6 key inputs were sourced (missing: SCIA pts scored, SCIA pts allowed, SCIA lineup rating or past seasons), so league averages filled the gaps. It was logged as a no-data call: graded and learned from, never offered as a bet.

review.title: How the ratings held up
review.body:
Storm came in with a league-average attack and a league-average defense (no scoring on file: rated at the league average), worth about 14 and 14 games of evidence. Projected to score 79.1, they scored 48 (−31.1 points, 39% under); projected to allow 70.3, they allowed 90 (+19.7 points, 28% over).

Leathernecks came in with a 12% below average attack and a 4% leakier than average defense (0-2, 62.5 scored and 77 allowed a game over 2 games), worth about 170 and 170 games of evidence. Projected to score 70.3, they scored 90 (+19.7 points, 28% over); projected to allow 79.1, they allowed 48 (−31.1 points, 39% under).

The bigger miss was Storm's scoring (-31.1 points against projection).

review.title: Where the result sat in the simulations
review.body:
Total: 138 against 149.4 projected (-11.4), about the 22nd percentile of the simulated totals (a typical game swings ±14.5).

Margin: Leathernecks by 42 against Storm by 8.8 projected, about the 99th percentile of the simulated margins (typical swing ±11).

An outlier: the simulations had a result this far off less than about 5% of the time, which usually means an input was wrong or missing, not just bad luck.

review.title: Situational factors, checked
review.body: Nothing situational moved this projection (rest, travel, form and conditions were all normal), so it came down to team strength.

Flagged going in: early-season numbers were thin; inputs were missing (SCIA pts scored, SCIA pts allowed, SCIA lineup rating or past seasons); there were no odds to check the projection against.

The projection missed by a lot, so those flags likely mattered here.
